title: Meeting Rooms
statement: Each meeting is [start, end) (the end time is free for another meeting to start). Return True if one person can attend all meetings, i.e. no two overlap.

large_tests.gen_code:
def gen():
    return [[[2 * i, 2 * i + 1] for i in range(50000)]]

hints.1_question: Two meetings conflict only if one starts before the other ends. Which pairs do you really need to compare?
hints.2_nudge: Sort by start time. After sorting, only neighbouring meetings can conflict first.
hints.3_big_hint: Sort; for i >= 1: if start[i] < end[i-1] return False. Return True.

known_bugs.name: does not sort
known_bugs.followup: Are the meetings given in time order? What do you compare for [7,10] followed by [2,4]?

known_bugs.name: treats back-to-back meetings as a clash (<=)
known_bugs.followup: A meeting ends at 2 and the next starts at 2. Can one person attend both?

known_bugs.name: compares every pair (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: How many pairs is that for 50000 meetings? What does sorting let you skip?

followups: What is the minimum number of rooms needed (problem 253)?
Why is checking neighbours after sorting enough?
